17.title: Trump after declaring cartels terrorist organizations: ‘Mexico is not going to like it’
17.description: Claudia Sheinbaum’s government faces the challenge of toughening its fight against drugs and showing results to prevent a potential US military incursion into Mexico
17.content:
The long-anticipated threat has become reality. On his first day in office, Donald Trump [signed an executive order](https://english.elpais.com/usa/elections/2025-01-21/trump-sweeps-away-biden-era-with-an-avalanche-of-decrees-against-immigration-the-green-agenda-and-diversity.html) designating Mexican drug cartels as terrorist organizations. “Mexico is not going to like it,” said the tycoon as he signed the decree in a sports arena in front of his supporters. According to specialists, the measure will give the U.S. government enormous powers that could violate Mexico’s sovereignty, resulting, for example, in drone attacks or military incursions on Mexican soil. [Claudia Sheinbaum’s government](https://english.elpais.com/international/2025-01-14/mexico-has-a-plan-sheinbaum-addresses-uncertainty-a-week-before-trump-returns-to-the-white-house.html), which has firmly stated the bilateral relationship will be one of cooperation and never subordination, will be under pressure to obtain results in its anti-drug policy, results that can be measured in Trump’s terms. The diplomatic relationship between the two countries, led in Mexico by a leftist president and in Washington by a politician more inclined to the xenophobic and racist right, is expected to be tense on such a priority issue as bilateral security and threatens to affect trade, an area in which both countries are deeply dependent.

Among the Republican president’s priority goals is the reduction of [fentanyl trafficking](https://english.elpais.com/usa/2025-01-09/fentanyl-the-key-to-war-and-peace-between-the-united-states-and-mexico.html), a drug that kills tens of thousands of Americans (in 2023, 70,000 people died from the synthetic opioid). Sheinbaum, who champions the discourse of tackling the drug-trafficking problem through social aid and addressing inequality, has also emphasized that among her priorities are undermining criminal structures and the seizure of drugs, coups that could give a respite to negotiations with Trump. In Sinaloa, where two factions of the Sinaloa Cartel, Los Chapitos and La Mayiza, loyal to Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, [have been waging an all-out war](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-12-14/the-drug-war-bleeding-sinaloa.html)for months that has left dozens dead, the Ministry of Security, headed by Omar García Harfuch, has captured several criminal leaders and seized a ton of fentanyl, [the largest cache of the drug ever impounded in Mexico](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-12-04/mexico-records-largest-fentanyl-seizure-in-history.html).

The list of terrorist organizations is managed by the U.S. State Department. Currently, 68 groups and individuals are included, from Hamas to the Colombian FARC guerrillas and [Shining Path in Peru](https://english.elpais.com/international/2023-08-30/us-declassifies-documents-chronicling-20-years-of-conflict-in-peru.html). While the main consequences of being on the list are financial — it makes it easier for the U.S. to block capital flows between countries and combat money laundering — there is also an aspect that excites both Republicans and Democrats: military intervention on Mexican soil with selective incursions aimed at damaging the cartels. A unilateral maneuver of this type would mean destroying decades of bilateral cooperation and intelligence exchange between the two governments to combat the historical problem of drug trafficking.

### A “soft invasion”

Academic Carlos Pérez-Ricart says that the order to classify the cartels as terrorists provides tools to the security, intelligence, and justice system of the United States to attack Mexican criminal organizations in a different way, and opens the door to a “soft invasion.” “In concrete terms, for Mexico, it implies that the U.S. intelligence ecosystem will already be on top of the country, which is something we had not seen until now: it will be the target of the United States intelligence agencies,” he warns. Author of the study _One Hundred Years of Spies and Drugs_, Pérez-Ricart maintains that, on the positive side of history, the new framework would also allow monitoring of private companies related to organized crime, from those that launder resources to arms companies that flood Mexico with illegal weapons and [provide the cartels with their enormous firepower](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-01-23/mexico-demands-investigation-into-us-military-grade-weapons-being-used-by-drug-cartels.html). “That can even be beneficial for the country,” he observes.

The researcher warns, however, that in relation to the fight against cartels, Mexico and the United States are pursuing two different and mutually exclusive objectives. “Mexico’s objective must always be focused on reducing the [violence generated by drug cartels](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-11-04/narco-violence-fear-and-politics-specter-of-terrorism-looms-over-relationship-between-mexico-and-the-united-states.html). The United States’ objective is to prevent drugs from reaching its country. There is a huge gap between both. Even by pursuing one, you weaken the other. And that is probably the tension in which the bilateral relationship is immersed,” he says. “If these new powers granted to the United States government are focused only on preventing drugs from reaching the U.S., they will continue to provoke violent dynamics in Mexico.”

Pérez-Ricart explains that drug trafficking organizations do not function in the same way as terrorist groups, and differ in their makeup, objectives, and methods. Therefore, he points out, they should not be approached in the same way. “The drug phenomenon is based on demand in the United States, not on supply. As long as the demand for drugs persists, it is impossible to think that the problem can be attacked at the source: Mexico,” he observes. The academic adds that, therefore, any project aimed at containing the problem only through the use of force “is destined to fail.” “[But] if this is going to imply a focused, intelligent use of disruption of violent organizations, and above all against the actors who swarm around drug-trafficking cells, I think it is good news,” he adds.

### Rise of militarism

Oswaldo Zavala, an academic and writer dedicated to the study of organized crime, qualifies the scope of Trump’s executive order and observes that, in terms of security, “Mexican sovereignty has always been violated by the U.S. anti-drug policy.” The researcher points out that the new tension around fentanyl is another stage in Mexico’s subordination to U.S. geopolitics, “[a] stormy, conflictive relationship of supposed cooperation, in quotation marks, that often resembles blackmail and extortion.”

For the author of _Cartels do not exist_, the main threat to Mexican sovereignty is the imposition from the United States and Europe of a militaristic approach to dealing with insecurity and migration. “When we talk about drug trafficking, we are talking about a way of expressing global militaristic policies, which in our country takes the form of combating organized crime, but which in other countries is called the fight against terrorism, or in countries like the United States, where the concepts of drug trafficking and terrorism are even mixed, as well as undocumented immigration,” he says.

Zavala states that the advance of militarism in Mexico is observed in “the normalized use of harassment and violence against the country’s own citizens.” The author exemplifies this with the containment of migratory flows by the army, military cyber espionage against civil society, the violation of human rights, the “disproportionate public spending on security,” or the lack of oversight over the Armed Forces. “We will not get rid of this problem if there is not a clear awareness that the main immediate problem for Mexican security has to do with our docile role, which allows the advance of national militarism in connection with global militarism,” he assesses.

Congressman Gildardo Pérez, from the Movimiento Ciudadano party, believes that Trump’s threats may have a greater impact because institutions in Mexico have been weakened, something for which he has blamed Morena, the ruling party. “These external pressures are due to an internal weakening. Trump takes advantage of the weakness we have in terms of the administration and delivery of justice,” he says. “The politicians of the last two decades [of the PAN, PRI and Morena] did not address the causes that were causing this institutional weakening,” he states. Beyond the criticism, [Sheinbaum’s response to Trump](https://english.elpais.com/international/2024-11-22/the-first-battle-claudia-sheinbaum-moves-against-trumps-immigration-policy.html) has been to reject submission, awakening a closing of ranks with the opposition parties. The conservative PAN, the majority opposition party, has rejected any possibility of “foreign interventionism.” Mexico awaits in tense calm the next move of the new American president.

¿Grupo Frontera apoya a Trump? La razón por la que los están cancelando
=======================================================================

Grupo Frontera es cancelado por un video que presuntamente los vincula con un apoyo a Donald Trump, presidente de Estados Unidos.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 3: Grupo Frontera fue vinculado con Donald Trump por esta razón. (Foto: Instagram @grupofrontera/Bloomberg)](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/resizer/v2/Q2Z5KQRRBNHTDKMINYSMYRWYGM.jpg?smart=true&auth=e40b0eb4e811f5949b82bb83f9194735d615f5420aa38d40ae462d94095572be&width=400&height=225&quality=85)

Grupo Frontera fue vinculado con Donald Trump por esta razón. (Foto: Instagram @grupofrontera/Bloomberg)

Por Redacción

enero 30, 2025 | 14:19 hrs

¿[Grupo Frontera es cancelado](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2023/08/12/grupo-frontera-agradece-a-amlo-reconocimiento-en-las-conferencias-mananeras-quieren-conocerlo/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2023/08/12/grupo-frontera-agradece-a-amlo-reconocimiento-en-las-conferencias-mananeras-quieren-conocerlo/")? La [banda de regional mexicano](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/29/que-dice-la-carta-de-lupillo-rivera-a-donald-trump/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/29/que-dice-la-carta-de-lupillo-rivera-a-donald-trump/") fue criticada por un presunto apoyo al **presidente de Estados Unidos**, pero, ¿qué fue lo que pasó?

Anteriormente, los intérpretes de ‘No se va’ vieron en primera fila la cancelación de otros músicos, así es, estamos hablando de [Yahritza y su Esencia](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2023/08/06/yahritza-y-su-esencia-como-se-hicieron-famosos/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2023/08/06/yahritza-y-su-esencia-como-se-hicieron-famosos/"), con quien compartieron créditos para la canción ‘Frágil’.

Recordemos que ‘No se va’ de **Grupo Frontera** fue una de las [canciones que aparecieron en la mañanera](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2024/09/30/que-canciones-aparecieron-en-las-mananeras-de-amlo-en-su-sexenio/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2024/09/30/que-canciones-aparecieron-en-las-mananeras-de-amlo-en-su-sexenio/") durante el mandato del expresidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador e incluso ofrecieron un [concierto en el Zócalo de la CDMX](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2024/09/15/que-bandas-tocaron-gratis-en-el-zocalo-en-15-de-septiembre-en-el-sexenio-de-amlo/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2024/09/15/que-bandas-tocaron-gratis-en-el-zocalo-en-15-de-septiembre-en-el-sexenio-de-amlo/") por festejos del 15 de septiembre de 2023.

![Image 4: alt default](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/resizer/v2/6X6FCN4A45DC5ABOXS5VADKZVM.jpg?auth=ba080330704ff0f4e35987bcef5725926481d5bf4928d7259ef16016471865d3&width=400&height=225&quality=85)

'no se va' de Grupo Frontera se escuchó en una de las mañaneras de AMLO. (Foto: Instagram @grupofrontera / Cuartoscuro)

Este es el motivo por el que cancelaron a Grupo Frontera
--------------------------------------------------------

Toda la [cancelación contra Grupo Frontera](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2023/04/16/bad-bunny-anuncia-nueva-cancion-con-grupo-frontera/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/entretenimiento/2023/04/16/bad-bunny-anuncia-nueva-cancion-con-grupo-frontera/") comenzó luego de la difusión de un **video en TikTok** donde la usuaria @sarahjasmine\_\_ aseguró que los integrantes de la **banda de regional mexicano** son integrantes del conjunto de personas denominadas ‘Latinos por Trump’.

Estos grupos de personas originarias de países de América Latina apoyan abiertamente al [Gobierno de Donald Trump](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/economia/2025/01/30/aranceles-de-mexico-a-donald-trump-a-que-sectores-le-puede-pegar-ildefonso-guajardo/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/economia/2025/01/30/aranceles-de-mexico-a-donald-trump-a-que-sectores-le-puede-pegar-ildefonso-guajardo/"), de acuerdo con la _BBC_.

Pero, ¿qué dice el video publicado en TikTok? “Regresemos a noviembre, hay un video donde se ve a **Grupo Frontera** diciendo que votan por Trump, ahora que se está cancelando a diferentes influencers latinos que apoyan a Donald, debo hablar de esto porque los vi”, comienza a decir la joven en inglés.

[![Image 5: Director de ‘Emilia Pérez’ afirma que el español es ‘un idioma modesto y de pobres’](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/resizer/v2/WNGPPWKMQJDOLJT6Y5ROLN7QPU.jpg?smart=true&auth=ab54b41cb3f8d5b88dca9178e4424aebe76d2bd72dbfccb0f6a07b50d10f7006&width=200&height=112&quality=85)](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/29/jacques-audiard-director-de-emilia-perez-opina-sobre-el-idioma-espanol/ "Director de ‘Emilia Pérez’ afirma que el español es ‘un idioma modesto y de pobres’")[Director de ‘Emilia Pérez’ afirma que el español es ‘un idioma modesto y de pobres’ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/29/jacques-audiard-director-de-emilia-perez-opina-sobre-el-idioma-espanol/ "Director de ‘Emilia Pérez’ afirma que el español es ‘un idioma modesto y de pobres’")

* * *

Sin embargo, después informa que la [banda Grupo Frontera](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2024/10/26/gran-premio-de-mexico-2024-que-celebridades-fueron-a-la-carrera-en-el-autodromo/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2024/10/26/gran-premio-de-mexico-2024-que-celebridades-fueron-a-la-carrera-en-el-autodromo/") borró las evidencias y los videos de sus diferentes redes sociales.

“Borraron los videos donde ello apoyan a Trump, pero ya, **no escuchen las canciones** ni vean sus videos de ellos porque votaron por Donald y ahora se están haciendo pend#jos, ellos son de este grupito de Latinos por Trump y aun así ellos van a México y quieren apoyo”, finalizó la usuaria @sarahjasmine\_\_.

Sumado a estas declaraciones, se difundió otro video donde aparece la abuela de [‘Payo’, vocalista de Grupo Frontera](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2023/08/16/grupo-frontera-habla-sobre-la-comida-mexicana/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2023/08/16/grupo-frontera-habla-sobre-la-comida-mexicana/"), donde aparece mientras baila la [canción YMCA, de Village People](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/14/que-artistas-cantaran-en-la-toma-de-protesta-de-donald-trump/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/14/que-artistas-cantaran-en-la-toma-de-protesta-de-donald-trump/"), grupo que estuvo presente en el cierre de campaña del republicano.

Sin embargo, es preciso mencionar que en el video de **‘La abuelita frontera**’ no aparece con ningún distintivo que demuestre apoyo al [presidente Donald Trump](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/opinion/enrique-quintana/2025/01/29/trump-el-mago-del-suspenso-y-del-acoso/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/opinion/enrique-quintana/2025/01/29/trump-el-mago-del-suspenso-y-del-acoso/").

Como respuesta a estos videos y rumores surgieron **memes en redes sociales** que se sumaron a la [cancelación de Grupo Frontera](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/tags/grupo-frontera/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/tags/grupo-frontera/").

![Image 6: Los memes de la cancelación de Grupo Frontera. (Captura: X )](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/resizer/v2/AOEJNCL54RFMZOI4XNJKKNEIX4.jpg?auth=c295b64eb8372781f0243fa9cca9e8872eebdf0fab31e2fdee1f31c24b91d324&width=400&height=225&quality=85)

Los memes de la cancelación de Grupo Frontera. (Captura: X )

¿Cuándo son los conciertos de Grupo Frontera para 2025?
-------------------------------------------------------

Adelaido Solía, [vocalista del grupo de regional mexicano](https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/28/jovanny-cadena-sufre-asalto-a-mano-armada-en-guadalajara-que-paso/ "https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/espectaculos/2025/01/28/jovanny-cadena-sufre-asalto-a-mano-armada-en-guadalajara-que-paso/"), compartió un video en su TikTok donde menciona que está ansioso por salir de gira nuevamente, sin embargo, no reveló fechas de próximos conciertos.

Las únicas presentaciones programadas de los **intérpretes de ‘El amor de su vida**’ para 2025 son dos, estos son los datos de cada una de ellas de acuerdo con Ticketmaster:

*   14 de marzo: Moody Anmphiteathre en Austin, Texas.
*   16 de marzo: NRG Stadium, Houston, Texas.

Is Grupo Frontera Now Cancelled? Controversy Explained
======================================================

Fans are turning their backs on this Spanish-language rock band after some recent drama.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By [Klein Felt](https://thedirect.com/about/klein-felt/)Posted: February 06, 2025

![Image 4: Grupo Frontera](https://images.thedirect.com/media/article_full/grupo-frontera-cancelled.jpg)

Supporters of Grupo Frontera are aghast as the band finds themselves awash in controversy with some calling for them to be canceled.

The Regional Mexican band from Edinburg, Texas, will be known to some for their ultra-viral hit "No Se Va," which picked up steam in 2022 and 2023 when it became a popular sound on the video-sharing platform TikTok.

As a band, they have released two full-length albums, including 2024's _Jugando a Que No Pasa Nada_, which featured music superstars George Strait and Morgan Wallen as special guest players.

Grupo Frontera Change.org Petition Explained
--------------------------------------------

![Image 5: Grupo Frontera standing in a mirror taking a selfie](https://images.thedirect.com/media/photos/grupo.png)

Grupo Frontera

Calls are ringing out for Grupo Frontera to be cancelled as accusations fly about the group potentially supporting U.S. President Donald Trump.

Specifically, a petition emerged online, asking that the band be removed from the 2025 Sueños Musical Festival lineup. Grupo Frontera is supposed to play the Chicago-based festival on Sunday, May 25, joining the likes of Shakira and Don Omar.

However, some fans believe they should be taken off the event (which celebrates Latin music and America's Latin population) as they claim they are Trump supporters and, in turn, **"support racism"**(per the [Change.org petition](https://www.change.org/p/remove-grupo-frontera-from-sue%C3%B1os-lineup)):

> "We want this because Grupo Frontera has been caught and found out to be Trump Supporters. This does not sit well with Latinos who may or may not be fans of the group but will not support racism.
> 
> 
> We Latinos stand united in boycotting Grupo Frontera and if they are not removed from the line-up, we will go as far as Boycotting Sueños Music Festival as well. La Raza Unida... Jamas sera Vencida!"

The petition has nearly 7000 signatures of its goal of 7500.

Grupo Frontera Controversy Explained: Do They Support Donald Trump?
-------------------------------------------------------------------

This Trump controversy surrounding the band stems from a TikTok video made by the grandparents of member Adelaido "Payo" Solís III where they were seen dancing to "YMCA" by The Village People after voting.

This came as the song had taken on a new meaning to many after it had been notably used by the U.S. President during his campaign.

The account was also allegedly seen liking several comments in the thread to the video expressing support for Trump. The video has since been deleted, but it was [screenshotted](https://vt.tiktok.com/ZS6oPWLqb/) by several users.

Many fans have extrapolated from this that, in turn, the band must support the president, which caused some to sour on the band. If that is the case, Grupo Frontera would hardly be the first big name to show their support for Trump, with [several A-list celebrities already having planted their flag in the President's camp](https://thedirect.com/culture/marvel-dc-hollywood-stars-endorsing-donald-trump).

Grupo Frontera Misinformation Debunked
--------------------------------------

As this controversy continued to burble online, various instances of misinformation about the band have started to make their way out as well.

One particularly viral [video](https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZT2rE5FNY/) sees the crowd at a Grupo Frontera concert seemingly cheering in support of Trump; however, the video looks to have been doctored in some way. An edit can be heard right as the song starts, with it abruptly cutting off the crowd's quote/unquote chants unrealistically.

Another popular [post](https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=pfbid02VGRTJr8xzPgmL1b8y2iyPQ8gSykpyVhyhmtdJTxLL3mSeaeSt7ueoMRConD6Vs2Nl&id=100094539907462) making the rounds is an alleged screenshot from the band's social media channels saying they **"do not care to be canceled:"**

> "Grupo Frontera responds saying that they do not care to be canceled in Mexico and that people envy them because they can be and walk in America peacefully."

Evidence of the post this image seems to have screenshotted can not be found anywhere, meaning it very easily may have been edited to spread misinformation about the situation.

Dozens of other instances of seemingly edited videos or photos surrounding the group have continued to pick up steam online, so fans should keep their eyes out and do their diligence before sharing one of these posts.

Do Grupo Frontera Support Donald Trump?
---------------------------------------

So, the is the question fans will almost surely be asking is: Does Grupo Frontera support Donald Trump?

Well, that answer is kind of unclear. In an interview with [El Pais](https://elpais.com/icon/2025-01-02/grupo-frontera-respetamos-las-leyes-estadounidenses-pero-apoyamos-a-los-inmigrantes-mexicanos-como-podemos.html) (translated from Spanish), the group addressed their thoughts on President Trump and his policies, saying while they **"respect the laws of the country,"**they have**"always supported immigrants:"**

> Juan Javier: "We rarely get involved in politics. It's very controversial for us and we just want to make music. But we've always supported immigrants. Last year we went to visit a center, we donated toys for the children. It's our neighborhood, after all."
> 
> 
> Alberto "Beto" Acosta: "We respect the laws of the country, but we do support immigrants as we can. We do things for the community. We donate toys for the children of the migrants who are there and who are being held captive."

While not directly addressing Donald Trump by name, this seems to be in direct response to the president's tough crackdown on immigrants living in the U.S. So, it would seem they at least disagree with that particular initiative, but whether they actively support Trump (or even voted for him) remains to be seen.

* * *

Grupo Frontera's latest release _Jugando a Que No Pasa Nada_ is available on streaming platforms worldwide. Read more about potential band drama in The Direct's breakdown of the Loveless controversy.

La [**música regional mexicana**](https://www.tvazteca.com/aztecauno/christian-nodal-aparece-nuevo-look-redes-felicitan-angela-aguilar-jap-notas-mt) está viviendo uno de sus mejores momentos, con nuevos talentos que fusionan lo tradicional con lo moderno. Sin embargo, no todo es color de rosa en esta historia de éxito. **Grupo Frontera**, la agrupación que conquistó los charts con "**No Se Va**", se encuentra en medio de una tormenta mediática que ha puesto en jaque su relación con sus seguidores.

[![Image 7: ¡Última llamada!: Este es el horario límite para votar por tu favorito en La Granja VIP HOY 19 de diciembre de](https://tvazteca.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f7c08c5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1332x821+0+40/resize/1200x740!/format/jpg/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Ftv-azteca-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F96%2F42%2Fc36f1ba14ceea4ac8ff86f987e89%2Faun-puedes-votar-este-es-el-horario-oficial-de-votaciones-en-la-granja-vip-para-este-viernes-19-de-diciembre-del-2025.jpg)](https://www.tvazteca.com/aztecauno/la-granja-vip/horario-oficial-votaciones-la-granja-vip-hoy/ "¡Última llamada!: Este es el horario límite para votar por tu favorito en La Granja VIP HOY 19 de diciembre de")

¿Qué fue lo que encendió la mecha?
----------------------------------

Todo comenzó con un video viral protagonizado por **'La Abuela Frontera'**, la abuela de uno de los integrantes del grupo, donde aparentemente celebraba lo que sus críticos interpretaron como un apoyo a ahora presidente de Estados Unidos. Este momento, aparentemente inocente, desató una [avalancha de críticas en **redes sociales**](https://www.tvazteca.com/aztecauno/mujer-convierte-gemela-belinda-tras-cirugia-estetica-lor-notas-mt) que ha puesto al grupo texano en una posición complicada.
